title: EU AI Act OpenRAG: Chunking a Law by Its Legal Structure, Not Sliding Windows
hook: Most RAG corpora chunk text with sliding character windows. This one chunks the EU AI Act by its actual legal structure and ships it as a single SQLite file.
key_points: Chunks Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 by legal structure, not sliding windows: one chunk per article paragraph, recital, Article 3 definition, or annex point.
Chapter, section, and provision metadata are stored separately from the chunk text.
933 total chunks, each paired with a normalized 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 embedding.
Ships as a single downloadable SQLite database, with exact EUR-Lex links and Article 113 application-date metadata attached.
content_html: A Reddit poster released "EU AI Act OpenRAG," a ready-to-use corpus of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 built specifically for RAG and legal-NLP experimentation. The interesting design choice: instead of the usual sliding character-window chunking, the corpus is segmented by the law's own structure — one chunk per article paragraph, one per recital, one per definition in Article 3, one per annex point.
extra_html: The result is a single SQLite file holding 933 structurally-aware chunks, each with a normalized 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 embedding, plus separately-stored chapter/section/provision metadata, exact EUR-Lex links, and Article 113 application-date info. For anyone building a legal-RAG demo or benchmarking retrieval on regulatory text, it's a drop-in dataset that sidesteps the usual chunk-boundary mess of splitting legal documents by character count. Posted to r/MachineLearning, July 2026 — see the thread for the download.

related.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
related.hook: Why force a model to memorize everything? RAG lets it look things up — fetch relevant documents, then answer from that evidence instead of frozen weights alone.

related.title: The EU AI Act
related.hook: The EU's answer to regulating AI: sort systems by how much risk they pose, then scale the rules to match — from outright bans to no rules at all.

related.title: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR)
related.hook: Keyword search misses answers that use different words. DPR embeds questions and passages into one vector space and retrieves by meaning — the backbone of modern vector search.

flashcards.prompt: How does OpenRAG's chunking strategy differ from typical sliding-window RAG chunking?
flashcards.back_html: It chunks along the Regulation's actual legal structure — one chunk per article paragraph, recital, Article 3 definition, or annex point — instead of fixed-size character windows.

flashcards.prompt: What embedding does each of the 933 chunks carry?

choices.text: No embedding — only the EUR-Lex link

flashcards.explanation_html: Every chunk in the SQLite database is paired with a normalized 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 embedding, ready for dense retrieval.

flashcards.prompt: Where is chapter/section/provision metadata stored relative to the chunk text?

choices.text: Separately, alongside the chunk rather than embedded in it
Concatenated directly into the chunk text before embedding

flashcards.explanation_html: The project keeps structural metadata (chapter, section, provision, Article 113 application dates, EUR-Lex links) in separate fields rather than mixing it into the text that gets embedded.
